thm:main/thm:gap are NP-hardness statements. conclusion.tex L40-55 says the graph is 'computable in deterministic polynomial time'; prop:affine-games and lem:unweighted are also deterministic. The Lean comparator requires a TM2ComputableInPolyTime map from binary 3SAT with noBound < alpha*yesBound, and its solution is sorry-free. So a BQP algorithm with fixed worst-case (or, after amplification, expected) ratio alpha > alpha_GW decides 3SAT, giving NP ⊆ BQP; the instances are galactic (|X|^T 2^{2^{(n+1)T}} vertices), but that does not affect the implication.

Core holds: the companion's cor:algorithm discharges EAMS Assumption 2 (a strictly increasing zero-temperature minimizer), giving an unconditional C(eps)n^2 SK optimizer, and its full-support theorem is Lean-checked conditional on a minimizer. Corrections: (i) Basso et al.'s 'p=11 beats all assumption-free classical algorithms' (0.6408 vs 2/pi) is about Max-Cut on large-girth D-regular graphs, not SK. The relevant classical algorithm there is EAMS 2023 (RSA), whose Assumption 1 is the same full-support statement, so the claim is obsolete there too, but only by inference. (ii) Montanari 2019's assumption is the positive-temperature one, discharged by Lopatto (arXiv 2607.11756, Jul 2026), and Chen (2607.18032, Jul 20 2026) proved the zero-temperature fact before the Sep 27 companion, so 'independently' should read 'earlier'.
